concept: Graph Community Detection Algorithms for RAG
summary: Graph clustering mechanics including Leiden, Louvain, and Infomap for constructing hierarchical community summaries in retrieval pipelines.

related.concept: Labeled Property Graph vs RDF Triplestore Storage Models
Graph Indexing and Adjacency Traversal Engines
GraphRAG Local and Global Community Summarization

facts.text: The Leiden algorithm resolves Louvain's fundamental defect of producing disconnected or weakly connected communities by introducing an explicit sub-community refinement step that guarantees partition connectivity.

Hierarchical community detection partitions large knowledge graphs into multi-scale clusters (from fine-grained sub-communities C3 to macro-thematic clusters C0), establishing the structured partition hierarchy required for multi-level GraphRAG summarization.

Modularity optimization (Newman-Girvan modularity Q) exhibits a resolution limit where communities smaller than sqrt(2L) cannot be resolved, necessitating Constant Potts Model (CPM) or resolution parameter tuning in RAG pipelines.
